subject: POC kickoff & hands-on: load test & benchmark session scheduling
messages:
From: Daniel Powell <dpowell@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff - hands-on load/benchmark session

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team (platform & infra) is excited to get a hands-on POC going. We want to run a combined session: an onboarding/kickoff + a focused load/benchmark run to validate throughput targets and latency SLOs.

High-level asks:
- 90 minute hands-on working session with access to the test harness
- Review of prompt routing and KV cache behavior
- Throughput validation up to ~800 reqs/min with tails measured at p95/p99

Are you available for a kickoff the week of June 8? We can do early mornings PST or mid-day EST. Also looping in procurement for any contract/PO questions.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

Attachment: initial-acme-requirements.docx (see summary below)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Powell <dpowell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - hands-on load/benchmark session

Hi Daniel — great to hear, and happy to run this.

Thanks for the asks. Proposed plan:
- 90 min hands-on kickoff + load run (we'll allocate a dedicated GPU pool for the session)
- Agenda: 1) quick architecture & prompt routing review (15 min), 2) test harness walkthrough & warm-up (15 min), 3) 45 min controlled throughput ramp + targeted SLO checks, 4) wrap + next steps (15 min)

Available slots we can offer:
- Wed, June 10 — 08:30-10:00 PT
- Thu, June 11 — 11:00-12:30 PT
- Mon, June 15 — 09:00-10:30 PT

Can you confirm which works best? I attached a draft POC load plan and the test-harness instructions we'll use. Also please share the team members who need access so we can provision tokens and an isolated namespace.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-load-plan.xlsx, test-harness-instructions.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - internal coordination

Looping in internal ops details. Stephanie — I can own the test harness orchestration and result capture (workbook templates). Dylan — can you confirm we can reserve a 4-GPU pool (A100-type) for a 2-hour window and a fallback 2-GPU pool if capacity spikes? Also which model variant should we stage (fp16 quantized vs 8-bit) — Daniel asked for throughput to ~800 reqs/min.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - internal ops confirmation

We can reserve the 4xA100 pool for the slot. Fallback 2xA100 is doable but will increase tail latency — we'll document expected p95/p99 deltas. For model: start with the fp16 (default) runtime, and keep an 8-bit quantized variant ready if they want cost-optimized runs. I'll pre-stage the model weights and pin the version to avoid drift during the test.

I'll also prepare a short runbook for the team: commands to trigger bursts, how to collect KV cache snapshots, and links to the dashboard that shows token-level cost breakdowns.

—Dylan
